But another, related force a policy often buried deep in course catalogs called 'grade forgivenessl' 一 is helping raise GPAs. Grade forgiveness allows students tO retake a course in which they received a IOW grade, and the most recent grade or the highest grade is the only one that counts in calculating a student's overall GPA. The use Of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent yea rs, as colleges continue tO dO their utmost tO keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates. When this practice first started decades ago, it was usually limited tO freshmen, tO give them a second chance tO take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition tO college-level courses. But now most colleges, save fO r many selective campuses, allow all undergraduates, and even graduate students, tO get their IOW grades forgiven. According to Paragraph 5, grade forgiveness enables colleges to ______.
A. boost their student enrollments.
B. improve their teaching quality.
C. meet local governments' needs.
D. obtain more financial support.

Text 2

The use Of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent yea rs, as colleges continue tO dO their utmost tO keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates. steps: 考点：阅读 Text 2·词义猜测题，考查 aligned 一词在上下文中的具体含义，须由前后文的逻辑关系定词义，不能只凭词典义硬套。

定位原文（Text 2 末段）："Since students and parents expect a college degree to lead to a job, it is in the best interest of a school to turn out graduates who are as qualified as possible — or at least appear to be. On this, students' and colleges' incentives seem to be aligned."

Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein is mentioned because it
A. fascinates AI scientists all over the world.
B. has remained popular for as long as 200 years.
C. involves some concerns raised by AI today.
D. has sparked serious ethical controversies.

Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea Of robots that would IOOk, move, and respond like humans, similar tO those recently depicted O n popular sci-fi TV series such as "WestworId" and TYumans." Just ow people think is still fa r tOO complex tO be understood, | et alone reproduced, says David EagIeman, a Stanford Un ive rsity neuroscientist. "We a re Just in a situation where there are no good theories explaining what consciousness actually is and how you could ever build a machine tO get there. But that doesn't mean crucial ethical issues involving AI aren't at hand. The coming use Of autonomous vehicles, fO r example, poses thorny ethical questions. Their reactions may be a complex combination Of instant reflexes, input from past driving experiences, and what their eyes and ea rs tell them in that moment. AI "vision" tOday is not nearly a S sophisticated a S that Of humans. And tO anticipate eve ry imaginable driving situation is a difficult programming problem. AIong with Singapore, other governments and mega-corporations are beginning tO establish their OW n guidelines. Britain is setting up a data ethics center. lndia released its AI ethics strategy this spring. On Ju n e 7 Google pledged not tO "design O r deploy AI" that would cause "overall harm," or tO develop AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms. 比 also pledged not tO deploy AI whose use would violate international laws O r human rights. steps: 考点：细节理解题，考查作者在首段提及《弗兰肯斯坦》的用意，关键是读懂 foreshadow（预示）的含义。

排除 B：原文只交代今年距小说出版恰好两百年（exactly two centuries），并未说它两百年来一直流行（has remained popular），属过度推断。
排除 D：原文说小说"预示"（foreshadow）了伦理问题，而不是小说本身"引发了严重的伦理争议"（sparked serious ethical controversies），与文意不符。
故正确答案为 C。

steps: 考点：细节推理题（题干补全型）。题干以 autonomous vehicles 为关键词，定位到原文第三段，依据该段对难度的表述判断「解决方案」目前处于什么状态。
